tone_statements.quote: 3.3 Tones The tone system of Pe is not well recorded, but it can be assumed to be similar to Tarok with three level tones and rising and falling.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 3.3 Tones, p. 5 (also p. 2: 'In general, tones are not marked, although the data was taped and they will be added when time permits.')

sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 3.3 Tones p. 5: 'The tone system of Pe is not well recorded, but it can be assumed to be similar to Tarok with three level tones and rising and falling.' Phonology otherwise = vowels, consonants, palatalisation/labialisation, homorganic nasals.

tone.quote: 3.3 Tones The tone system of Pe is not well recorded, but it can be assumed to be similar to Tarok with three level tones and rising and falling.
tone.locator: sec. 3.3 Tones, p. 5 (also p. 2: 'In general, tones are not marked, although the data was taped and they will be added when time permits.')
tone.n_tones: Assumed 3 level + rising + falling (by analogy with Tarok; not analysed)
tone.says: Sec. 3.3 'Tones' (p. 5) is two lines: the tone system is not well recorded and is assumed to be like Tarok, i.e. three level tones plus rising and falling; intro (p. 2) says tones are in general not marked in the data though recordings exist; sec. 4.1 notes singular/plural pairs distinguished only by prefix tone (i-low sg vs i pl, 'tone-raising.. widely attested in Plateau'). No tone analysis, no minimal pairs, no TBU discussion.

Sec. 6.2 Phonology pp. 10-11: consonant and vowel inventories from a 348-item wordlist; 'there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological features, nor has there been an effort to determine the phonemic status of phones'. Wordlist (App. E) marks some tones, no stress.

tone.quote: In this section, we will discuss some initial, tentative observations on the phonology of Pye. It is considered tentative because it is based on a small data set and there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological features, nor has there been an effort to determine the phonemic status of phones.
tone.locator: sec. 6.2 Phonology, p. 9 (Tables 1-2 follow on p. 10); the repeated sentence is in the Appendix E: Wordlist introduction, p. 29
